title: How to Create an AI Influencer for Ads (2026 Guide)
summary: How to create an AI influencer for brand ads: well-known examples, a 7-step build flow, tools, listed costs of about $6.68 per pass.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **To create an AI influencer for ads, build a character sheet, generate scenes from it with an image model, animate them with image-to-video, add a voice, and test the cuts.**
- An AI influencer is a computer-generated character used in marketing like a human creator. Lil Miquela, Aitana López and Shudu Gram are the best-known examples.
- Generation is cheap: about **$6.68** for 20 stills and ten 10 second clips at listed prices, before retries. Consistency and review take the time.
- For ad use, the character works best as the on-screen presenter in short UGC-style videos.


## What an AI influencer is


An AI influencer, also called a virtual influencer, is a fictional character made with software that appears on social media and in brand marketing the way a human creator would. Wikipedia defines a virtual influencer as a computer-generated fictional character used for marketing, usually on social media in place of human influencers.


The older versions were built with CGI and motion capture. Current ones are built with image and video generation models. That drop in production cost is why brands now treat a virtual creator as a repeatable ad asset.

## How to create an AI influencer for ads, step by step


This is the production flow for a brand that wants a repeatable on-screen creator, not a one-off image.


1. **Define the persona.** Write one paragraph: age range, look, voice, what the character cares about, and which product problem they speak to. Pick a face that fits the audience, not a generic model.
2. **Build a character sheet.** Generate one clean reference set: front, three-quarter and profile views, plus two outfits. Save these images. Every later generation uses them as references.
3. **Generate the stills.** Make the ad scenes with an image model that accepts reference images, holding the character sheet constant and changing only the scene, product and ratio.
4. **Animate with image to video.** Turn each approved still into a 5 to 10 second clip with an image-to-video model. Keep one simple motion per clip.
5. **Add the voice.** Add speech with a lip-sync or avatar tool, or record a voiceover and sync it. Keep scripts to one or two sentences per clip.
6. **Write the ad around the creator.** Open with a hook in the first two seconds, show the product in use, and close with one offer line. Cut the clips together and add captions.
7. **Test and review.** Run three to five creator variants against each other, and check every frame for face drift, product accuracy and text errors before launch.


### Step detail: the character sheet


The sheet is what holds the face together. Google's Nano Banana models accept up to 14 reference images per prompt. On Nano Banana 2 and 2.1 that can include up to 4 character images and on Nano Banana Pro up to 5, per Google's documentation. Feed the sheet in every time. A prompt like "the woman from the references, holding the water bottle in a gym locker room, phone-camera framing, 9:16" gives you a scene with the same person. See[Nano Banana 2 for ad creatives](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-for-ads) for the model details.


### Step detail: stills to video


Take each approved still into an image-to-video model and ask for one simple motion, such as a head turn, a product lift or a smile. Ranked tools and clip lengths are in[best image to video AI generators for ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/image-to-video-ai) . Tools with lip sync, such as the ones in the[PixVerse review](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/pixverse-review) , can add speech from a portrait and audio. The[AI avatar generator](https://www.sprites.ai/ai-avatar-generator) page covers the talking-presenter format.


## What it costs


Using vendor prices listed on November 9, 2026: Google lists Nano Banana Pro at $0.134 per 1K or 2K image, and PixVerse lists V6 at $0.040 per second at 720p without audio.

Add a tool subscription if you use a consumer app rather than an API, and editing time. A marketer who already has a character sheet can produce a week of ads in an afternoon. A freelancer UGC creator is a very different cost and speed.


## Where an AI influencer works in ads, and where it does not


- **Works:** demo-style UGC for products where the product is the star, such as apps, accessories and beauty tools. See[AI influencer ads for fashion](https://www.sprites.ai/ai-influencer-ads/fashion) .
- **Works:** a recurring brand character across many ad variants, where a consistent face builds recognition.
- **Weak:** claims that need a real customer, such as before and after results, reviews and testimonials. An invented person cannot honestly be a customer.
- **Weak:** long takes. Face drift gets more likely as a clip gets longer, so cut to short shots.


One platform line: check the AI-content label option on each ad platform when you upload. Google's image models also embed an invisible SynthID watermark.

## FAQ


### What is an AI influencer?


An AI influencer is a computer-generated character that posts and appears in marketing like a human creator. Wikipedia describes a virtual influencer as a computer-generated fictional character used for marketing, most often on social media in place of human influencers. Brands use them for sponsored posts and, increasingly, as the on-screen creator in video ads.


### How do I create an AI influencer?


Define a persona, build a character sheet of reference images, generate scenes with an image model that accepts references, animate them with image-to-video, add a voice with a lip-sync tool, then cut and test the ads. The hard part is keeping the face the same across every image and clip.


### What are examples of AI influencers?


Lil Miquela began in 2016 as an Instagram profile for a CGI character created by Trevor McFedries and Sara DeCou. Aitana López is an AI-generated influencer from Barcelona created by the agency The Clueless. Shudu Gram is a computer-generated model described as the world's first digital supermodel.


### How much does it cost to make an AI influencer?


The generation cost is small. At Google's listed $0.134 per Nano Banana Pro image and PixVerse's listed $0.040 per second for V6 at 720p, 20 stills and ten 10 second clips cost about $6.68 before retries. The real cost is time spent on consistency, review and editing, plus any tool subscriptions.


### Can an AI influencer run in paid ads?


Yes. Many brands use an AI character as the presenter in Meta, TikTok and YouTube ads, since the creative is just image or video. Check each platform's AI-content label option when you upload, and review every frame before it goes live.


### How do I keep an AI influencer's face consistent?


Use a fixed character sheet as reference images in every generation, and prefer models that support character references. Google's Nano Banana models accept up to 4 or 5 character reference images depending on the model. Reject any output where the face drifts instead of fixing it later.
